_doc: Per-sector macro sensitivity used by the regime overlay and the stress panel (engine/regime_overlay.py). Coefficients are analyst judgments (economist audit, 2 Nov 2026), not estimated from data; each has a one-line rationale. rate: 0 none, 1 some, 2 high (floating-rate/EBLR, leveraged or financed demand). crude: -2 crude/fuel is a major cost .. +1 producer benefits. inr: -2 import-dependent inputs (weak rupee hurts) .. +2 net exporter (weak rupee helps). cyclical: demand falls with the cycle; defensives do not. wpi_group: OEA WPI/PPI NIC-2 group used for the margin driver and the credit deflator. margin_scope: group = margin driver scored; display = group-level only (shown, not scored, because the sector is a narrow slice of the group); none = no mapped series (unknown). deflator: WPI group for price-adjusting bank credit; ALL = headline WPI for broad trade/MSME books; null = no deflator (gap left nominal). demand_beta (derived in code): defensive 0.4, govt 0.6, consumption/export 1.0, capex 1.2 when cyclical; scales the demand stress shock. defensive_floor: score cannot fall below Caution (45) without hard evidence (GNPA trend -1 or credit-gap red flag). deflator_coarse: the WPI group is much broader than the sector (e.g. 'other manufacturing' is dominated by gold/silver jewellery prices, not polished diamonds), so the credit gap uses the larger of the nominal and deflated gaps.

mmf_textiles.why: PTA/MEG and polyester yarn track crude; inputs priced in USD; thin weaver margins; working-capital heavy MSME borrowers on EBLR loans.

cotton_textiles.why: Cotton is domestic but globally priced; yarn is ~30% exported so a weak rupee helps; WC-heavy cotton stocking is rate-sensitive.

apparel.why: Net exporter with low import content: weak rupee helps; US tariff exposure is a policy risk not scored here.

diamonds.why: Rough is imported and polished exported, so the rupee roughly nets out; very high working capital and USD credit lines make it rate-sensitive; discretionary demand.

chemicals_dyes.why: Crude/naphtha-derived feedstocks, partly imported; exports offset only part of the rupee hit.

petrochem.why: Feedstock is crude/naphtha/gas; prices pass through with a lag.

pharma.why: Defensive demand; formulation exporters gain from a weak rupee, partly offset by imported APIs/KSMs; low WC sensitivity to rates. Defensive floor: essential, non-discretionary demand with export diversification; output/credit-gap/margin signals alone cannot push it below Caution, only a rising GNPA trend or a red-flag credit gap can.

ceramics.why: Gas/LNG is the main cost and is imported; demand tied to housing; export market softening.

plastics.why: Polymer resins track crude and are partly imported; small processors cannot pass costs quickly.

engineering.why: Capex-cycle demand; rate rises delay orders; mixed import/export content.

metals.why: Coking coal imported, steel prices global; capex/construction demand; leveraged secondary producers.

electronics.why: High imported component content: weak rupee raises costs; PLI support not scored.

auto_components.why: Vehicle demand is financed and rate-sensitive (autos lag in tightening); fuel cost dampens demand; exports offset imports.

paper.why: Packaging-led steady demand; energy and imported pulp are costs.

food_processing.why: Staple demand is defensive; margins depend on farm prices.

commercial_real_estate.why: Most rate-sensitive sector: valuations and lease-rental discounting reprice with rates.

beverages.why: Defensive consumption; packaging and fuel costs.

leather.why: Export-oriented footwear and leather goods; weak rupee helps; WC heavy.

wood_plywood.why: Housing-linked demand; imported timber and chemicals (resin).

refining.why: Crude is both input and output price; margin is the crack spread, captured by the margin driver, not a fixed sign.

fertiliser.why: Administered prices and subsidy receivables: judged borrower by borrower, regime not applied.

cement.why: Petcoke/coal and diesel freight costs rise with crude; housing and infra demand slow in tightening.

glass.why: Gas-fired furnaces; imported soda ash; housing/auto demand.

nonferrous_brass.why: Copper/zinc scrap imported in USD; WC heavy MSME clusters.

electrical_eq.why: T&D capex cycle; copper/steel inputs; utility receivables lengthen in tightening.

other_transport.why: Two-wheelers are financed purchases; rate- and fuel-sensitive demand.

handicrafts.why: Export demand; weak rupee helps; discretionary.

sugar.why: Administered cane price and ethanol pricing drive margins; regime overlay not applied (proxy).

edible_oil.why: About 60% of edible oil is imported: a weak rupee raises costs; import-duty policy drives margins; WC heavy.

tea.why: Defensive demand; fuel and wage costs; auction prices not modelled.

cashew.why: Raw nuts imported, kernels exported, so the rupee roughly nets out; WC heavy.

mining.why: Commodity producers benefit from higher global prices and a weak rupee.

construction.why: EBLR-linked, receivable-heavy contractors; bitumen and diesel costs; government payment cycles.

power.why: Regulated returns; imported coal and gas cost pass-through lags; DISCOM receivables.

renewables.why: Long-tenor project debt reprices with rates; imported modules.

telecom.why: Defensive subscription demand; imported network equipment.

roads.why: Project debt rate-sensitive; bitumen tracks crude.

agriculture.why: Defensive; diesel and fertiliser costs; monsoon risk not modelled.

msme_micro_small.why: EBLR-linked loans reprice within a quarter; thin margins absorb input-cost inflation (Brickwork Oct-2026).

msme_medium.why: EBLR-linked loans; input-cost absorption; mixed exposure.

wholesale_trade.why: Working-capital lending at floating rates; credit growth inflates with prices.

transport_ops.why: Diesel is the largest cost; financed fleets on floating rates.

tourism_hotels.why: Discretionary; weak rupee helps inbound tourism and holds back outbound.

aviation.why: ATF tracks crude, aircraft leases are in USD; highly levered.

software_it.why: USD revenue, rupee costs: weak rupee helps; low leverage.

nbfc.why: Borrowing costs reprice faster than assets; funding-sensitive in tightening.

rice_milling.why: Exports gain from weak rupee; export-policy risk not scored.

marine_meat_dairy.why: Seafood exports gain from weak rupee; fuel cost for fishing fleets.

shipping.why: USD freight revenue; bunker fuel cost.

airports.why: Regulated tariffs; traffic linked to fuel-driven airfares.

housing_finance.why: Mortgage demand and funding costs both rate-sensitive.

other_services.why: Health and education demand is defensive.
